name: welcome-mashup-logo
why: Plain-terminal welcome banner intentionally draws oh-my-pig's 24×11 half-block π-plus-pig mashup (with vertically centred wordmark and Piglet version `v<PigletVersion>`) instead of omp's 12×5 block π (`v19.1.1`).

name: welcome-tip-block
why: Welcome tips are chosen randomly per launch and filtered to registered commands; each side's joined tip text is validated against its source tips list and 72-column wrap.

name: host-startup-notices
pig_regex: ^(?:\[Extensions\]|  path|    builtin:piglet|  builtin:piglet| Piglet oh-my-pig hid 2 tools from the registry:| - built-in tools: powershell, ls \(the Piglet's `tools` list does not name it\))$
why: PiG host prints `[Extensions]` and `Piglet oh-my-pig hid 2 tools from the registry: powershell, ls` unless the user sets `quietStartup` (a Piglet manifest cannot set it and `sdk.Context.GetSettings()` is read-only); matched on the pig side only with the exact hidden tool list pinned.

name: host-markdown-code-indent
ref_term: Host assistant markdown fenced code block indentation
why: PiG's built-in assistant markdown renderer indents fenced code lines by 3 columns (`markdown.codeBlockIndent` default `"  "` + 1 column host margin), which a Piglet manifest or extension cannot override.

name: host-ctrl-o-status-text
why: Emitted directly by PiG host `InteractiveMode.setAllToolsExpanded`; extensions cannot override this status message.

name: host-provider-error-text
pig_regex: ^(?: Error: 400: \{"message":"Proof simulated provider| error","type":"invalid_request_error"\}| If this looks like a pig bug, /bug sends a report to the developers\.)$
why: Strictly host-drawn transcript error lines (`Error: 400: ...`, `/bug` hint on pig) and omp's wrapped `raw-http-request=<log>.json` dump path (matched as one logical wrapped line from `raw-http-request=` through `.json` on omp's side only); does NOT match the port-drawn pinned `✘ 400 ...` banner line.

name: host-stock-editor-frame
why: PiG's stock editor draws top/bottom full-width border rules around the input row (omitting omp's bare `╰─` prompt gutter) because installing a delegated `sdk.EditorComponent` breaks `/` & `@` autocomplete and deadlocks shutdown; matched structurally at the active dock tail only (omp side restricted to bare `╰─`).

name: omp-stale-pre-resize-frame
why: omp keeps a stale pre-resize copy of its active dock block in scrollback/screen after width resize while PiG clears cleanly via CSI 2J + CSI 3J; matched strictly on the omp side only when the stale block equals the active dock re-wrapped at the old width.

name: host-user-prompt-bubble-colour
why: PiG host owns user message rendering and does not expose theme registration for the `#0f1216` (`rgb:15;18;22`) user bubble background and `#e5e5e7` foreground.

name: host-assistant-markdown-colour
why: PiG host owns assistant markdown & thinking text colours (emitting default/256-colour system tokens `38;5;1,3,4,5,6`, plus `faint+italic` on thinking text) while omp applies its titanium markdown palette.

name: host-notify-info-colour
ref_term: Plan mode enabled. Plan file: local://PLAN.md
why: PiG renders `ctx.Notify(..., "info")` transcript status notices (such as `Plan mode enabled. Plan file: local://PLAN.md`) with host `ActiveTheme().Fg("dim", msg)` (`\x1b[39m\x1b[2m`, SGR faint + default fg) in `internal/codingagent/interactive_chat.go:583-604`, while omp renders dim truecolor `rgb:107;114;128` without SGR faint.

name: blank-welcome-and-startup-notices
why: Host startup notices (`[Extensions]` and `hid 2 tools`) and welcome banner/tip wrapping change surrounding blank separator rows inside that classified hunk.

name: blank-markdown-code-block
ref_term: Host assistant markdown fenced code block indentation
blank lines inside fenced code blocks
ref_subject: blank lines inside fenced code blocks
why: PiG's assistant markdown code-block hunk includes the blank line separating lines inside the fenced Go code block.

name: blank-host-stock-editor-input-row
why: PiG's stock editor draws an empty input row between its top and bottom full-width border rules.

name: blank-omp-stale-pre-resize-frame
why: omp's stale pre-resize dock copy includes internal blank separator rows on the omp side only.

name: omp-resize-alt-screen-borrow
why: omp briefly borrows the alternate screen (`CSI ?1049h`...`?1049l`) strictly between width-resize start and settle (`tui.ts:2085-2197`) and nowhere else; verified from raw stream byte offsets.
